summary: Read-only web research sweep on Home Assistant to ROS2 integration options (MQTT bridges, add-on vs integration, prior art, safety patterns), then synthesise
logs: Sweeping six research angles in parallel

synthesis.executive_summary: The evidence favours plain MQTT. Home Assistant 2026.10 needs no new code: MQTT device discovery creates the arm's entities, and stock scripts can publish a goal, wait on an mqtt trigger for ack and result with timeouts, and return a typed response. The ROS 2 machine runs either ika mqtt_client 2.5.0 plus a small gateway node, or one purpose-built paho node. No path removes a 150 to 400 line ROS-side node, because acknowledgement, de-duplication, heartbeat watchdog and action handling are behavioural. A custom integration is justified only for typed services with responses, and should then be MQTT-based, not rosbridge-based. A ROS 2 runtime inside an HA add-on is poor (DDS, host networking); a bridge-host add-on over rosbridge is viable but unauthenticated. Two findings reshape the safety design: the stock Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 enforces no topic ACLs, and HA does not await SUBACK, so acks must be retained with expiry. No winner is picked before the interview.

options.name: 1. Plain MQTT: HA's built-in MQTT integration plus a bridge on the ROS 2 machine
options.what_it_is: HA side is configuration only. ROS side is either (a) ika-rwth-aachen/mqtt_client 2.5.0 YAML (JSON or primitive topic mapping, retained publish, LWT, user/pass, TLS) plus a 150 to 250 line rclpy gateway node for discovery payload, birth/online, command validation, ack and dedupe, action lifecycle and heartbeat watchdog; or (b) one purpose-built 250 to 400 line rclpy node with paho-mqtt 2.1.0 doing all of it in one process. HA consumes via device-based discovery (homeassistant/device/<id>/config), availability topic with LWT, sensors with expire_after, button/select/number/text for commands, event entity for results, and scripts using mqtt.publish, wait_for_trigger (mqtt trigger templated on command_id), timeout, and stop with response_variable.
pros: Zero HA-side code; MQTT integration is platinum core code with no breaking discovery change in 2026.10
Broker, credentials and TLS already exist on HA OS; DDS never leaves the ROS machine
Every living precedent (OASIS, MowgliNext, April 2026 patrol robot) chose this shape
mqtt_client is apt-released for Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical and Rolling, institutionally maintained
Full request/response flow verified in HA 2026.10.1 source: trigger.payload_json, wait.completed, response_variable
MQTT 3.1.1 clients coexist with HA's v5 session on Mosquitto 2.1.2 (verified)
cons: Not code-free on the ROS side: discovery, birth, ack, dedupe, watchdog and action handling always need a node
mqtt_client JSON mode is 2.5 months old, has no CI tests, no public field reports, silently zeroes missing fields and omits 1-byte arrays over 100 elements
HA does not await SUBACK (0.5 s debounce), so a fast non-retained ack can be missed; ROS side must publish ack and result retained with MQTT v5 message expiry on per-command topics
mqtt.publish is admin-only since 2026.10: non-admin dashboard users must go through automations or discovery entities, not script buttons
Stock Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 does not enforce acl_file (issue #4571), so any authenticated MQTT client can publish to the command topics
No request/response or action semantics in MQTT itself; the contract (command_id, max_age, retained replies) is bespoke design
options.effort: Low on HA (YAML and dashboard); medium on ROS (one node of 150 to 400 lines plus optional mqtt_client YAML); a weekend to a working prototype, longer for safety hardening
options.maintenance_burden: Lowest of all options: a topic contract and one ROS node. HA monthly releases have not broken discovery since 2024.11; watch the 2027.6 publish API change only if an integration is added later
options.best_when: HA issues a fixed menu of named tasks or setpoints and reads summarised state; the user accepts owning one small ROS 2 node; broker-side authorisation is not required or is enforced at the application layer

options.name: 2. Thin MQTT-based custom integration (HACS) on top of option 1
options.what_it_is: A custom_components/<domain> package that rides HA's own MQTT connection via homeassistant.components.mqtt helpers (async_publish, async_subscribe, async_wait_for_mqtt_client, async_on_subscribe_done), subscribes to ack and result topics before publishing, awaits an asyncio.Future per command_id, and registers a typed service (ros.run_action) with SupportsResponse plus optional event or sensor entities. Mirrors the tasmota and pglab dependency pattern. Roughly 8 to 12 files and 600 to 1,200 lines including tests.
pros: Closes the subscribe race in code and gives schema-validated services with responses and a device model
Keeps broker authentication and TLS; no second transport
Non-admin users can call the integration's own service
Good test tooling (pytest-homeassistant-custom-component, integration_blueprint)
cons: Only adds value if stock scripts prove insufficient; the ROS-side node is still required unchanged
Must track HA developer churn: entity lifecycle hooks (2027.11), device registry single config entry, config entry listener deprecation (2026.12), publish API None removal (2027.6)
HACS needs a public GitHub repository with releases, brand assets and version in manifest
Cannot import rclpy: HA core is Alpine/musl Python 3.14, rclpy is not on PyPI
options.effort: Medium to high: config flow, services, strings, tests, HACS packaging
options.maintenance_burden: Medium: a handful of mechanical deprecations per year, but every HA release must be checked
options.best_when: Many concurrent long actions, cancellation semantics, typed validation or a polished device model are hard requirements, or a non-admin household must start actions from scripts

options.name: 3. Bridge-host HA add-on with no ROS 2 runtime (rosbridge WebSocket client), including the Node-RED prototype variant
options.what_it_is: A Supervisor-managed container on the internal hassio network (no host_network) that connects to rosbridge_suite on the ROS machine (port 9090, JSON over WebSocket, topics, services and actions natively), gets Mosquitto credentials via the Supervisor services API or talks to HA over ws://supervisor/core/websocket, and maps goals, feedback and GoalStatus to HA entities or MQTT topics. Fast prototype: the community Node-RED add-on (v22.1.0, host_network true) plus node-red-contrib-ros2-suite 0.2.0 installed through npm_packages.
pros: Native ROS 2 actions and services without designing an MQTT action protocol
Protocol logic lives in an HA-managed artefact, independent of HA core monthly churn
rosbridge is maintained (4.2.1 Aug 2026; Humble 2.0.8 has send_action_goal), apt-installed, no ROS code to write for transport
Can bind rosbridge to one interface, use WSS, and ufw-restrict 9090 to the HA OS IP
cons: rosbridge has no authentication (removed 2021) and globs are server-wide; security is purely network-level
Still needs a ROS-side watchdog node: rosbridge has no safe-state concept, websocket_ping_interval defaults to 0
Greenfield: no existing HA add-on, sidecar or HACS component packages a rosbridge client; roslibpy says ROS 2 support is still in progress
node-red-contrib-ros2-suite is single-author, first published 2026-10-04, zero users; Node-RED add-on runs host_network with manager role
Docker-published ports bypass ufw on the ROS host if rosbridge runs in a container
options.effort: Medium: Dockerfile (2026.04 BuildKit pattern), config.yaml with mqtt:need, aarch64 and amd64 images, client with reconnect and action lifecycle; prototype in Node-RED in hours
options.maintenance_burden: Medium: add-on API is stable, but you maintain a bespoke client plus rosbridge version matching per distro
options.best_when: The owner is HA-centric, wants code on the HA box rather than the ROS box, needs native actions and feedback, and the LAN segment is trusted

options.name: 4. ROS 2 runtime inside an HA add-on (DDS participant on the HA OS host)
options.what_it_is: An add-on built FROM ros:<distro> with host_network true (multicast) or ROS_STATIC_PEERS or Fast DDS discovery server, joining the arm's DDS domain from the HA machine and translating to HA via MQTT or the Supervisor API.
pros: Technically possible: official ros images exist for amd64 and arm64v8, add-ons allow host_network and privileged capabilities
Full rclpy access to topics, services and actions
cons: Needs host networking, which HA's add-on security guidance says not to do; HAOS firewall behaviour for DDS UDP is UNVERIFIED
Couples the HA box to the arm's exact distro and RMW; multi-hundred-megabyte image and upgrades on HA OS
No authentication without SROS2; second DDS participant on the LAN
Still ends in an MQTT or HA API translation step; no prior art anywhere
Contradicts the stated split (HA triggers, ROS 2 controls)
options.maintenance_burden: High: two ROS 2 installs to keep in step plus add-on builds
options.best_when: Practically never for this setup; only if DDS-native access from the HA host were a hard requirement

options.name: 5. rosbridge-based custom integration, or AppDaemon/pyscript scripting over rosbridge
options.what_it_is: A from-scratch aiohttp WebSocket client speaking the rosbridge JSON protocol inside HA core (no HA-ready library exists), or roslibpy inside the AppDaemon add-on, or pyscript with allow_all_imports.
pros: Native actions and services
AppDaemon plus roslibpy is the fastest de-risking experiment with no HA integration and no ROS code
cons: Unauthenticated path from HA core to the arm; adds a second transport beside the broker
Twisted-based roslibpy sits badly in HA's event loop; the only precedent (KamilaLis/rosrobot, 2018) was abandoned
AppDaemon releases are slow by its own admission; pyscript long-lived websocket viability UNVERIFIED
Entities are second-class compared with discovery or a real integration
options.maintenance_burden: Medium to high, and dependent on volunteer projects
options.best_when: Only as a throwaway prototype, or if MQTT is ruled out entirely

options.name: 6. Other transports: zenoh, Foxglove bridge, HTTP shim
options.what_it_is: zenoh-bridge-ros2dds or rmw_zenoh with zenoh-plugin-mqtt (an MQTT broker, not a client) bridged from Mosquitto; Foxglove bridge (binary protocol); or a bespoke rclpy plus FastAPI REST shim with HA rest_command and webhooks.
pros: zenoh has strong TLS, mTLS and ACLs and monthly releases through 2026
HTTP design needs no new HA software (rest_command, webhook-triggered template sensors, REST API)
cons: zenoh payloads are CDR and rmw_zenoh keys embed type hashes, so a translating node is still required; zenoh-plugin-mqtt lacks retained messages and QoS 1/2 and would need a Mosquitto bridge hop; RMW is not zenoh by default on any distro
Foxglove: no maintained Python client (ws-protocol archived Aug 2025), no auth, binds 0.0.0.0
HTTP shim: no maintained ROS 2 REST project (ROStful 2019, ros2-web-bridge 2022); if a node is written anyway, MQTT is cheaper
options.effort: High for zenoh and Foxglove; medium-low for an HTTP shim
options.maintenance_burden: High for zenoh (router, version matching, RMW switch); medium for a bespoke shim
options.best_when: The arm stack already runs rmw_zenoh (zenoh), or debugging only (Foxglove); otherwise not recommended

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: ika-rwth-aachen/mqtt_client (C++ component node)
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: v2.5.0 released 2026-07-22; apt ros-$ROS_DISTRO-mqtt-client for humble, jazzy, kilted, lyrical, rolling; MIT; 300 stars; 11 to 12 open issues; last commit 2026-07-22
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Topics only (services and actions 'not planned', issue #72). JSON mode new in 2.5.0 via rosx_introspection 3.1.2: ros_type mandatory, no CI tests, no public field use, missing JSON fields decode to zeros, arrays of 1-byte types over 100 elements silently dropped, outbound JSON path has no exception guard. Publishes nothing on connect (no birth, no reaction to homeassistant/status). MQTT 3.1.1 only, no WebSockets. Docker images amd64 only; use apt on arm64. Retained inbound commands are not filtered. Still needs a gateway node for discovery, ack, watchdog and actions.

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: Purpose-built rclpy node with paho-mqtt 2.1.0 (pattern, not a package)
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.repo: Reference implementations: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mowglinext/mowglinext/main/ros2/src/mowgli_monitoring/src/mqtt_bridge_node.cpp (C++, libmosquitto, 2,076 lines) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eigendude/OASIS/main/oasis_home/oasis_home/nodes/hass_mqtt_bridge_node.py (Python, paho, 319 lines)
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: paho-mqtt 2.1.0 (PyPI 2024-04-29) is what HA 2026.10 itself runs on Python 3.14.2; packaged in Ubuntu 26.04 and rosdep key python3-paho-mqtt; CI matrix added 3.13 and 3.14 in June 2026
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Everything is custom (250 to 400 lines estimated, UNVERIFIED): will plus on_connect birth and discovery republish, JointState to JSON via rosidl_runtime_py, command validation, dedupe, action client, ack/result, watchdog. Use CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2; pre-2024 examples break. aiomqtt 2.5.x plus rclpy AsyncNode is a Lyrical-only single-loop alternative; aiomqtt 3.0 is a breaking alpha.

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite (WebSocket JSON server on the ROS host)
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: Active (pushed 2026-10-05); humble 2.0.8, jazzy 2.7.1, kilted 3.3.1, rolling 4.2.1 (Aug 2026); actions since 2.0.0 (Oct 2024) including Humble branch
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: No authentication since 1.0.5 (2021). Mitigate with address:=<LAN IP>, certfile and keyfile for WSS, topics_glob/services_glob allowlists and a ufw rule for the HA OS IP. On Humble set call_services_in_new_thread and send_action_goals_in_new_thread true. Needs an HA-side client that does not exist yet (option 3 or 5).

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: blanpa/node-red-contrib-ros2-suite (Node-RED palette over rosbridge)
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: 0.2.0 published 2026-10-04; single author; 0 stars, 0 weekly downloads; depends only on ws; nodes for topics, services, actions (client and server), params, TF
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Prototype only. Installable into the community Node-RED add-on via npm_packages. No track record; bus factor of one.

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: eclipse-zenoh zenoh-plugin-mqtt plus zenoh-plugin-ros2dds or rmw_zenoh
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: 1.10.1 released 2026-09-07 (both); rmw_zenoh Tier 1 since Kilted but not default on any distro
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Not recommended: zenoh-plugin-mqtt is a broker, not a client of Mosquitto; no retained messages (issue #6 open since 2022), no QoS 1/2; payloads are CDR so HA cannot parse them without a translator; rmw_zenohd plugin loading UNVERIFIED.

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: groove-x/mqtt_bridge
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: ROS 1 only (lunar 0.2.1, 2020), declared unmaintained, README redirects to mqtt_client
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Ruled out. Anyone recommending it for ROS 2 is working from pre-2024 information.

recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.name: Small Python bridges: Eagle-Creative/FlexComm_bridge, reidlo5135/ros-mqtt-bridge, COGNIMANEU pilot02
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.status: 1 to 2 stars each, single author, 2025 to 2026 pushes, none in rosdistro
recommended_ros2_bridge_candidates.caveats: Reference code only (rclpy message_to_ordereddict plus paho pattern); not credible production dependencies.

safety_patterns: Physical e-stop stays hardwired to the arm controller (IEC 60204-1 Stop Cat 0 or 1, ISO 13850); nothing in HA or MQTT is labelled E-Stop. MQTT carries at most a non-safety 'inhibit' or 'system stop' (NFPA 79 10.7.2.3 forbids software graphic e-stops; UR safety I/O is paired PLd hardware). Sources: industrialmonitordirect NFPA 79 article (May 2026), UR SW10.15 manual, robotics.stackexchange 101882.

Fail safe by absence: HA publishes a heartbeat every 1 to 2 s (time_pattern automation plus mqtt.publish); a watchdog node on the ROS host treats silence beyond 3 to 5 s as loss of permission, refuses new goals, cancels the active goal or publishes 'stop' on MoveIt's trajectory_execution_event, and reports 'inhibited'. The watchdog never lives in HA. Precedent: OSHWA Protective Stop design, 10 Hz heartbeats, 'every failure mode degrades to no message'. ros-safety/software_watchdogs (last push 2024-01-30) is a reference design only.

Broker-level liveness is slow: Mosquitto closes a connection only after 1.5 x keepalive (90 s at the 60 s default). Lower keepalive on both ends (HA minimum 15 s; mqtt_client client.keep_alive_interval) and keep the application heartbeat.

Status contract: retained robot/<arm>/status {state, ts, seq} plus LWT 'offline' retained; HA availability_topic with payload_available 'online'; sensor expire_after catches a bridge that is connected but silent. Include a session sequence (Sparkplug bdSeq idea) so HA discards in-flight expectations after a bridge restart. Birth 'online' must be published by a ROS node (mqtt_client never does).

Commands: never retained, QoS 1, carrying command_id (UUID), issued_at and max_age; the ROS gateway rejects stale commands (covers queued replays after reconnect) and keeps a dedupe window (covers QoS 1 duplicates); keep clean_session true on the ROS side so a restart never drains a backlog of motion commands. MowgliNext rejects retained deliveries on command topics for the same reason.

Replies: ack and result published retained on per-command topics with an MQTT v5 message expiry (60 to 300 s), because HA does not await SUBACK and would otherwise miss a sub-200 ms ack. Use the MQTT event entity (ignores retained replays) for dashboards and loose automations; do not use a retained topic as a persistent automation trigger (re-fires on every HA restart).

Action mapping over MQTT mirrors rosbridge: cmd/goal, cmd/cancel, goal/<id>/ack, goal/<id>/feedback (QoS 0, throttled), goal/<id>/result with action_msgs/GoalStatus (4 succeeded, 5 canceled, 6 aborted), and a retained goal/current for state after restart.
Validate command schemas in the ROS node, not in the bridge: mqtt_client's JSON decoder turns a typo into an all-zeros but valid message.

Stop hooks that exist in the stack: MoveIt trajectory_execution_event 'stop' (preempt and cancel all controllers); MoveIt Servo incoming_command_timeout 0.1 s; joint_trajectory_controller cmd_timeout and constraints.decelerate_on_cancel; a custom action server that on cancel sends a single-point trajectory at the current position (ROS Discourse 42773).

Entity choice for safety: buttons for named motions rather than a select (MowgliNext: picking an item cannot start motion); automations rather than dashboard-launched scripts for non-admin users (mqtt.publish is admin-only since 2026.10).

Authorisation: the stock Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 does not enforce acl_file (go-auth superuser bypass via nginx returning 200), so either enforce at the application layer (nonce or HMAC in the command, allowlist of command names on the ROS side), pin the add-on at 6.5.2, run a standalone broker, or wait for addons PR #4831. On any broker, the shared 'addons' account is one identity for every add-on using the Supervisor MQTT service.

Standards posture for a home: ISO 10218-1/-2:2025 (which absorbed ISO/TS 15066) and ISO 13482 do not apply as obligations to a domestic arm, but their principles transfer: safety functions belong to the robot's safety-rated hardware; collaboration is an application property, so assess who can be in reach when HA fires a trigger; cybersecurity now counts as safety, so use authenticated MQTT and TLS if Wi-Fi is shared.

Network expectations: Mosquitto adds sub-millisecond latency and QoS 1 costs one LAN round trip (1 to 5 ms); MQTT is not a real-time channel, so all motion loops stay in ROS 2 and HA only issues goals and permission. Measure with mqtt_client inject_timestamp on the actual LAN.
prior_art: MowgliNext (ROS 2 Lyrical robot mower, pushed 2026-10-13): purpose-built C++ libmosquitto node publishing device-based HA discovery (v1.5.0, 5 Oct 2026), retained status, availability via LWT, discovery republished on reconnect and on homeassistant/status online, retained commands rejected, buttons not selects, fire-and-forget with status polling, stale-subscription recovery (issue #644). docs/MQTT_CONTROL.md is the best current template. Never mentions mqtt_client (reason undocumented).

OASIS (eigendude, ROS 2 smart-home OS, pushed 2026-08-30): HA via MQTT Statestream plus a 319-line Python paho node; author abandoned mqtt_client on 2025-04-22 for layering and latency reasons ('the problem with a HA component is the ROS dependency'); reported HA events arriving late and out of order (2025-05-01); no discovery, no LWT.
HA community, April 2026 patrol robot with small arm: 'ROS2 to MQTT bridge to HA', camera, device_tracker, button entities and named high-level actions; no code published.
KamilaLis/rosrobot (2018): the only HA custom integration for ROS ever published; ROS 1, roslibpy over rosbridge, Twisted reactor in a thread inside HA, one commit, abandoned. Stale.

Ken McElhinney servo arm (2021, ROS 1): groove-x mqtt_bridge failed on sensor_msgs/JointState; author flattened to a one-way comma-separated string. Only robot-arm plus HA example found. Stale, and the gap-fill found no source for a JointState failure with mqtt_client.
openHAB iot_bridge (2015, ROS 1, REST): sensor-triggers-robot use case solved by a ROS-side node calling the home platform's API. Stale.
EMQX 'MQTT and micro-ROS' (2024-07-10): micro-ROS stays on UDP to the agent; mqtt_client bridges to the broker; micro-ROS has no MQTT transport.
Zenoh gist by JEnoch (2023): zigbee2mqtt data into ROS 2 via zenoh-bridge-mqtt plus zenoh-bridge-dds; data in, not commands out.

No HA add-on, HACS integration or Docker sidecar packaging ROS 2, rosbridge or roslibpy for Home Assistant exists (multiple GitHub API searches returned zero on 2026-10-13); no HA forum thread on ROS 2 arms in 2024 or 2025.
version_facts: Home Assistant Core 2026.10.0 released 2026-10-07, 2026.10.1 on 2026-10-10; REQUIRED_PYTHON_VER (3, 14, 2); core container is Alpine 3.24 / Python 3.14; MQTT integration pins paho-mqtt==2.1.0, platinum, single_config_entry.

2026.10 MQTT changes: mqtt.publish and mqtt.dump require an administrator (PR #182045, merged 2026-09-14); MQTT lawn mower stop action. Automations run without user context and are unaffected; scripts started by a non-admin fail at the publish step; discovery entities publish internally and are unaffected.

HA requires an MQTT 5 broker since 2026.6 (PR #169759 merged 2026-05-05, silent migration via PR #172500; repair issue only if v5 fails, breaks_in 2027.1.0). This governs HA's own client only; v3.1.1 third-party clients coexist on Mosquitto.

Other 2026 MQTT integration changes: object_id discovery option removed in 2026.4 (use default_entity_id); time/date/datetime platforms and discovery at any QoS in 2026.5; message_expiry_interval on publish (v5 only); infrared platform in 2026.8; dedicated MQTT settings page with publish and subscribe tools in 2026.9. Device-based discovery since 2024.11; MQTT device subentries since mid-2025 (21 platforms, no event, update or device_trigger, no export to discovery payload).

HA MQTT internals at 2026.10.1: DEFAULT_PROTOCOL 5, DEFAULT_QOS 0, keepalive 60 (minimum 15), birth/will on homeassistant/status, subscriptions debounced 0.5 s then 0.1 s with no SUBACK wait (mqtt.async_on_subscribe_done added 2025-11-23 for integrations), mqtt trigger has no retain filter, event entity ignores retained replays.

Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 (master, 2026-09-10): Mosquitto 2.1.2, mosquitto-go-auth 3.0.0 (upstream archived 2025-06-08), Debian 13, aarch64 and amd64 only (32-bit dropped in 7.0.0), ports 1883/1884/8883/8884, no anonymous logins, logins list, customize include_dir. acl_file via customize is NOT enforced on 7.x (issues #4571 open since 2026-04-17, #4721; PR #4831 unmerged). Mosquitto 2.1.0 (2026-01-29) deprecated acl_file and password_file (removal at 3.0) and set max_packet_size default to 2,000,000 bytes.

ROS 2 distributions: Lyrical Luth released 2026-05-22 (LTS to May 2031, Ubuntu 26.04 Python 3.14); Kilted Kaiju released 2025-05-23, EOL November or December 2026 (sources disagree); Jazzy Jalisco 2024-05-23 (LTS to May 2029, Ubuntu 24.04 Python 3.12); Humble Hawksbill 2022-05-23 (LTS to May 2027, Ubuntu 22.04 Python 3.10); Iron EOL. Next: Makoa Mata-mata May 2027.

Default RMW is Fast DDS on every active distro including Lyrical; rmw_zenoh Tier 1 since Kilted but opt-in and needs a router (tcp 7447, multicast scouting off); Fast DDS discovery server removes the multicast requirement.

mqtt_client 2.5.0 (2026-07-22) on humble, jazzy, kilted, lyrical, rolling; depends on rosx_introspection 3.1.2 (released, last commit 2026-09-12), libpaho-mqtt-dev, libpaho-mqttpp-dev; MQTT 3.1.1 via Paho default; ros2 branch removed, everything on main.

rosbridge_suite: humble 2.0.8, jazzy 2.7.1, kilted 3.3.1, rolling 4.2.1 (all 2026-08-12); BSON dropped in 4.1.0; actions since 2.0.0 (2024-10-08); authentication removed in 1.0.5 (2021). roslibpy 2.1.0 (PyPI 2026-06-30), ROS 2 support 'still in progress'.

paho-mqtt 2.1.0 (PyPI 2024-04-29, no release since; master active Sep to Oct 2026, CI covers 3.9 to 3.14); VERSION1 callbacks deprecated. aiomqtt 2.5.1 (2026-03-05, needs paho 2.1); aiomqtt 3.0.0a1 (2026-04-02) replaces paho with the Rust mqtt5 library (needs Python 3.11+), breaking.

rclpy: LifecycleNode since Humble; experimental EventsExecutor since Kilted; experimental AsyncNode since Lyrical (Python 3.12+, not thread-safe, no actions yet). rclpy is not on PyPI; ros-python-wheels (Kilted, glibc) and roswell 0.1.0 (alpha, manylinux) cannot load on HA's musl Python.

HA add-ons ('apps'): aarch64 and amd64 only; Supervisor 2026.04.0 removed the default BUILD_FROM argument (BuildKit migration, blog 2026-04-02); internal bridge network 172.30.32.0/23 with masquerade (outbound LAN TCP works without host_network); Supervisor GET /services/mqtt supplies broker host, port, username 'addons' and password to add-ons declaring mqtt:need.
Node-RED community add-on v22.1.0 (2026-10-03), host_network true, npm_packages option; AppDaemon add-on 0.19.2 (2026-08-30), AppDaemon 4.5.13 (2026-01-19); pyscript 2.1.0 (2026-08-11).

interview_questions.question: What should Home Assistant be able to tell the arms to do? 1 A fixed menu of named tasks or poses (start job A, home, open gripper). 2 Numeric setpoints such as a pose, speed or joint target. 3 Free trajectories or continuous teleoperation. 4 A mix of 1 and 2.
interview_questions.why: This is the single biggest fork: options 1 and 4 map to MQTT button, select, number and text entities over topics; option 2 needs structured JSON; option 3 argues for keeping all motion in ROS 2 and exposing only triggers, and makes MQTT a poor fit for the live part.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether mqtt_client topics suffice or an action gateway is needed; which HA entity platforms to request via discovery; whether a thin integration is ever worth it.

interview_questions.question: When HA starts an arm task, does the automation need the outcome back in the same run? 1 Yes, it must branch on success, failure or timeout. 2 Fire and forget is fine; HA watches a status sensor or event later. 3 Yes, and it must also be able to cancel a running task.
interview_questions.why: Stock HA scripts can do 1 and 3 over MQTT (wait_for_trigger with command_id, response_variable), but only if the ROS side publishes retained, expiring acks; option 2 removes the ack protocol entirely.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether the ROS node implements goal, ack, result and cancel topics; whether per-command retained replies with MQTT v5 expiry are required; whether an MQTT-based custom integration is ever justified.

interview_questions.question: Is a small custom ROS 2 node on the arm machine acceptable to write and maintain? 1 Yes, that is the natural place for it. 2 Only off-the-shelf packages on the ROS side; any custom code should sit on the HA box. 3 No custom code anywhere if at all possible.
interview_questions.why: Every safe design needs a watchdog and command gateway on the ROS host, so option 2 pushes towards the bridge-host add-on over rosbridge plus a minimal watchdog, and option 3 is not achievable for a moving arm; the answer sets which machine owns the maintenance.
interview_questions.changes_what: MQTT with a ROS-side node (options 1 or 2) versus bridge-host add-on (option 3); and whether to use mqtt_client plus a tiny gateway or one purpose-built node.

interview_questions.question: Which ROS 2 distribution and OS does the arm machine run? 1 Humble on Ubuntu 22.04. 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04. 3 Kilted on Ubuntu 24.04. 4 Lyrical on Ubuntu 26.04. 5 Not decided yet.
interview_questions.why: Fixes Python (3.10, 3.12 or 3.14), rclpy features (AsyncNode only on Lyrical), rosbridge version (2.0.8 Humble needs threading flags for actions), apt availability of mqtt_client 2.5.0, and Kilted's end of life in November or December 2026.
interview_questions.changes_what: Bridge library choice (paho sync versus aiomqtt plus AsyncNode), launch arguments, and whether a distro move must be planned first.

interview_questions.question: Can a person or pet be within reach of an arm while it moves after an HA trigger? 1 No, it is enclosed or interlocked. 2 Yes, but someone is always present and watching. 3 Yes, and it may run unattended (for example overnight or while people sleep).
interview_questions.why: Sets the required safety layer: option 1 allows a simple software inhibit; options 2 and 3 require the arm's own protective-stop or monitored-standstill functions to be wired and a heartbeat watchdog before HA may start motion.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether HA is allowed to start unattended motion at all; watchdog timeout; whether an MQTT inhibit must also drive a relay into a hardware safety input.

interview_questions.question: Which arms are they (make and model), and what safety inputs do they have? 1 A dedicated hardware e-stop or safeguard-stop input (UR-style paired safety I/O). 2 Only an e-stop button on the controller. 3 Hobby or servo arms with no safety hardware. 4 Not sure, need to check.
interview_questions.why: Decides whether the ROS-side inhibit can drive a relay into a hardware stop input or must remain software-only, and whether the arm driver exposes ros2_control, MoveIt or a vendor action.
interview_questions.changes_what: Safety design (hardware versus software stop), the action interface the gateway node must call, and which stop hooks (trajectory_execution_event, cmd_timeout) exist.

interview_questions.question: If the HA heartbeat stops arriving at the arm, what should happen? 1 Inhibit new motion only; let the current task finish. 2 Stop the current motion as well. 3 Nothing; HA going away should not affect the arm.
interview_questions.why: Fail-safe-by-absence is the core pattern; option 2 needs a cancel path into the controller (preempt plus hold position), option 3 means HA is purely advisory and the watchdog can be dropped.
interview_questions.changes_what: Watchdog behaviour and timeout in the ROS node; which controller stop hook is used; whether HA availability drives any arm state.

interview_questions.question: The stock Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 does not enforce topic ACLs, so any authenticated MQTT client (Zigbee2MQTT, ESPHome, Tasmota, any HA user) could publish arm commands. Which is acceptable? 1 Fine on this trusted LAN. 2 Enforce on the ROS side instead (command allowlist, nonce or HMAC in the payload). 3 Broker-side ACLs are required: pin the add-on at 6.5.2, run a standalone broker, or wait for PR #4831. 4 This rules MQTT out for commands.
interview_questions.why: MQTT's claimed security advantage over rosbridge does not hold on the stock add-on today; the answer decides whether MQTT remains the transport and what authorisation layer the ROS node must implement.
interview_questions.changes_what: Transport choice; ROS node command validation design; broker deployment changes.

interview_questions.question: Will anyone who is not an HA administrator start arm actions from a dashboard or wall tablet? 1 Yes. 2 No, admins only.
interview_questions.why: mqtt.publish is admin-only since 2026.10, so a script started by a non-admin fails; commands must then flow through automations or MQTT discovery entities, or a custom integration with its own service.
interview_questions.changes_what: HA-side design of command entry points (automation plus input helpers, discovery buttons, or an integration service).

interview_questions.question: What arm state should HA see? 1 Discrete states and events only (idle, busy, error, job done). 2 Summarised state at about 1 Hz (current task, pose name, gripper, faults). 3 Live joint positions or pose at several Hz.
interview_questions.why: Options 1 and 2 are comfortable for MQTT entities and the recorder; option 3 needs JSON mode or a custom serialiser, throttling, QoS 0 non-retained topics, and recorder exclusions, and may argue against entities for the high-rate part.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether mqtt_client JSON mode is used, topic retain and QoS settings, recorder configuration, and whether the one prior JointState lesson matters.

interview_questions.question: Who should define the HA entities for the arm? 1 The ROS side publishes an MQTT device-discovery payload (entities appear automatically). 2 You create them by hand in the HA UI as MQTT device subentries. 3 Manual MQTT YAML in HA.
interview_questions.why: Discovery is the only route that supports event, update and device_trigger platforms and survives reinstalls; subentries cannot be exported to a discovery payload later, so the routes are not interchangeable.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether the ROS node carries the discovery JSON and birth-message logic; which platforms are available; who edits entity names and icons.

interview_questions.question: How are the two machines connected? 1 Wired Ethernet on the same switch. 2 One or both on Wi-Fi. 3 Across a mesh, VLAN or second subnet.
interview_questions.why: Sets heartbeat timeout margins, whether TLS on 8883 is warranted, whether DDS multicast would ever work (relevant only to option 4), and which rosbridge or broker firewall rules apply.
interview_questions.changes_what: Timeouts, TLS decision, and whether the DDS-in-add-on option can be dismissed outright.

interview_questions.question: Which software drives the arms inside ROS 2? 1 MoveIt 2. 2 ros2_control with joint_trajectory_controller directly. 3 A vendor ROS 2 driver with its own action or service. 4 LeRobot or another non-ROS stack with a ROS wrapper. 5 Not built yet.
interview_questions.why: The gateway node's action lifecycle, cancel path and stop hooks depend entirely on this interface; it also sets the QoS of state topics the bridge must match.
interview_questions.changes_what: Gateway implementation details, available stop mechanisms, and which state topics are meaningful to surface.

interview_questions.question: If a custom HA integration were ever built, is a public GitHub repository acceptable? 1 Yes. 2 No, private only.
interview_questions.why: HACS only works with public repositories with releases; a private-only requirement removes HACS distribution and leaves manual installation.
interview_questions.changes_what: Viability and packaging of option 2; otherwise no effect.

interview_questions.question: Are Node-RED, AppDaemon or pyscript already installed and in use on this HA instance? 1 Node-RED. 2 AppDaemon. 3 pyscript. 4 None of them.
interview_questions.why: An existing Node-RED add-on allows a same-week rosbridge prototype with the new ros2-suite palette; AppDaemon allows a roslibpy experiment; neither should be the production path, but either de-risks the design before code is written.
interview_questions.changes_what: Whether a throwaway prototype precedes the build and which tool it uses.

interview_questions.question: How many arms are there, and do they ever need coordinated motion from a single HA trigger? 1 One arm. 2 Several arms, independent tasks. 3 Several arms, coordinated as one job.
interview_questions.why: Coordination moves the goal, ack and status model from per-arm to per-job and belongs in a ROS 2 orchestrator, not in HA automations; it also affects discovery device structure and script mode (parallel).
interview_questions.changes_what: Topic layout (robot/<arm> versus job/<id>), where sequencing logic lives, and HA script concurrency.

interview_questions.question: What CPU architecture is each machine? 1 Both amd64. 2 HA OS on aarch64 (Pi or similar), ROS machine amd64. 3 ROS machine on arm64 (Jetson or Pi). 4 Other or unsure.
interview_questions.why: mqtt_client Docker images are amd64 only (apt works on arm64); add-on images must be built for aarch64 and amd64; a ROS 2 add-on image on a Pi is heavy.
interview_questions.changes_what: Install method for mqtt_client, add-on build matrix, and whether option 4 is ruled out on resources alone.

interview_questions.question: Which other MQTT clients are on the broker today, and do any use the shared 'addons' service account rather than their own login? 1 Zigbee2MQTT add-on. 2 ESPHome or Tasmota devices with their own logins. 3 Both. 4 None.
interview_questions.why: The 'addons' account is one identity for every add-on consuming the Supervisor MQTT service, so even a working ACL cannot separate them from the arm unless they get their own logins; it also sizes the blast radius of the unenforced-ACL finding.
interview_questions.changes_what: Broker credential layout, ACL design, and how much weight the authorisation question carries.

unverified_or_contradictory: Exact JSON text emitted by mqtt_client JSON mode for sensor_msgs/JointState and other types: structure is inferred from rosx_introspection source and round-trip tests, but no test asserts output text. UNVERIFIED until a live ros2 topic pub test; array and byte rendering edge cases likewise.
Kilted Kaiju end of life: 31 December 2026 (endoflife.date, ROS Releases page) versus November 2026 (REP 2000 heading). Unresolved.

Lyrical Luth Python version: 3.14 inferred from Ubuntu 26.04 packages (python3 3.14.3); no ROS primary source states it because REP 2000 has no Lyrical section yet. docs.ros.org was unreachable (Anubis bot wall) for every page.
Earlier claim that 'the one prior arm project broke on JointState' with mqtt_client: no source exists; the 2021 failure was with groove-x mqtt_bridge on ROS 1.

MowgliNext's reason for not using mqtt_client is undocumented (repository search returns nothing); the inferred reason is that discovery, birth, availability and command relay are not expressible in mqtt_client YAML.

Latency and ordering contradiction: benchmarks show sub-millisecond broker latency, but OASIS reported HA events arriving late, out of order and with jitter over a two-Python-node path (2025-05-01). Likely reconciled by Mosquitto max_inflight_messages 1 and avoiding double hops, but untested.

HA subscription-identifier nuance (warm exact-topic subscriptions receiving messages before SUBACK) is read from client.py at 2026.10.1 but not exercised against a live Mosquitto 2.1.2. Retained replies with expiry are the recommended mitigation regardless.

PR #182045 release notes say a non-admin manually triggering an automation fails; source reading shows automation.trigger creates a child Context without user_id, so it should pass. No test covers it. UNVERIFIED at runtime.
Mosquitto handling of an expiring MQTT v5 message queued for an offline v3.1.1 persistent session is undocumented; by spec expired messages are dropped for all subscribers.

Whether mosquitto_acl_file.so (the 2.1 plugin replacement for acl_file) is present in the HA add-on image is UNVERIFIED; one user report says loading it did not work. Behaviour of Supervisor-authenticated HA users under PR #4831 is UNVERIFIED (reading the diff, they would be denied all topics).

Whether rmw_zenohd can load the zenoh REST or MQTT plugins is UNVERIFIED (README silent, default router config has no plugins block); zenoh-plugin-ros2dds payload encoding is CDR by inference from a 2021 blog and a pycdr2 demo, not from a 2026 primary source.
HAOS firewall behaviour for inbound DDS UDP on a host-network add-on and the Supervisor security-rating deductions for host_network could not be verified (source files returned 404).
roslibpy ROS 2 action support: v2.0.0 release notes claim an action client, but the current README lists only ROS 1 actionlib and says ROS 2 support is still in progress. Treat as UNVERIFIED.
pyscript's suitability for a long-lived WebSocket (rosbridge client) is undocumented. UNVERIFIED.

paho.mqtt.python PR #916 (3.14 in CI) shows 12 of 13 checks passing; the failing check is unidentified. No 3.14 issue exists in the tracker, and HA 2026.10 runs paho 2.1.0 on Python 3.14.2, which is strong indirect evidence.

Sparkplug bdSeq and seq semantics come from vendor summaries (HiveMQ 2024); the Eclipse specification itself could not be read. ISO 10218:2025 Class I/II and PL d Cat 3 wording, and the ISO 13482 revision status, are UNVERIFIED (iso.org, A3 and TUV pages returned 403).
Effort estimates (mqtt_client YAML plus 150 to 250 line gateway; purpose-built node 250 to 400 lines; integration 600 to 1,200 lines) are derived from verified feature lists, not measured code.

Earlier research angle 6 stated MQTT-3-only libraries are 'ruled out' by HA's MQTT 5 requirement; the gap-fill shows this is incorrect for third-party clients on Mosquitto 2.1.2 (verified from Paho headers, mosquitto docs, a Mosquitto author reply from 2021 and an HA maintainer comment of 2026-08-31).

Pre-2024 sources used for background and flagged potentially stale: IBM mqtt-status-pattern (2014), openHAB iot_bridge (2015), rosbridge auth removal (2021), Control Design stop categories (2021), ROS Answers Docker multi-host thread (2020), 'Unconfigured DDS considered harmful' (2022), McElhinney servo arm (2021), mosquitto-dev interoperability reply (2021).

sweep_angles: ROS2-side MQTT bridges: every maintained package that bridges ROS2 topics/services/actions to MQTT, plus whether micro-ROS or zenoh offer an MQTT path. Research date 2026-10-13. All primary sources were fetched directly; dates are from GitHub API, ROS Index or release pages unless marked UNVERIFIED.

Home Assistant-side architecture options for coupling HA OS (2026.10.x, Mosquitto add-on) with a ROS2 machine on the same LAN: add-on (Supervisor container) vs custom integration (in-process Python, HACS) vs plain MQTT discovery vs AppDaemon/pyscript. Researched 2026-10-13 from developers.home-assistant.io, home-assistant.io, home-assistant/core and addons source, docs.ros.org source on GitHub, ROS Discourse and GitHub API metadata.

Prior art: who has connected Home Assistant to ROS or ROS 2, how (transport, direction, packaging), how recently, and what pitfalls they hit. Researched 2026-10-13, read-only, web search plus GitHub REST API and Discourse search JSON endpoints.

Safety and reliability patterns when Home Assistant (HA OS 2026.10.x, Mosquitto add-on) triggers physical robot arms controlled by ROS2 on a separate LAN host: heartbeat/watchdog over MQTT, e-stop and inhibit signalling, command acknowledgement and idempotency, mapping ROS2 actions onto MQTT, Mosquitto LAN latency/QoS, and a proportionate note on ISO 10218:2025 / ISO/TS 15066 for a home setting.

Alternatives to MQTT and the networking reality: rosbridge (websocket JSON) from HA, HTTP/REST or webhook shims in either direction, zenoh as transport, Foxglove bridge, and native DDS participation from HA OS. Context: HA OS 2026.10.x with the Mosquitto add-on on one machine, ROS 2 on a second LAN machine driving robotic arms, everything local.

Current version snapshot as of 2026-10-13: ROS 2 distributions, Home Assistant Core 2026.10 MQTT changes, the official Mosquitto add-on, Python MQTT client libraries, and rclpy API notes relevant to a small bridge node.

gaps.gap: No verified answer to whether the 'plain MQTT' option is configuration-only (ika-rwth-aachen/mqtt_client 2.5.0) or necessarily a purpose-built ROS 2 node. Angle 1 crowns mqtt_client the clear leader; angle 3's only two living precedents (OASIS, MowgliNext) abandoned or bypassed it and wrote their own paho/C++ node; angles 4 and 5 both conclude a custom node is needed anyway for actions, acks, dedupe and the heartbeat watchdog. Specific unverified facts: JSON-mode rendering of arrays, JointState and custom msgs (flagged UNVERIFIED in angle 1, and the one prior arm project broke on JointState); whether mqtt_client can emit a retained HA device-discovery payload and an LWT that HA accepts as availability; and whether its MQTT 3.1.1-only client is acceptable now that HA requires an MQTT 5 broker (angle 6 says MQTT-3-only libraries are ruled out, angle 1 recommends one, angle 4 left it UNVERIFIED).
gaps.why_it_matters: The effort and maintenance comparison that puts MQTT ahead of a custom integration assumes near-zero code on both sides. If mqtt_client cannot carry the HA contract, 'plain MQTT' becomes 'write and maintain a 300-line ROS 2 node with safety logic', which is the same order of effort as a thin custom integration. That changes which option is cheapest and which machine (ROS or HA) owns the code the user must maintain.
gaps.research_prompt: Research date 2026-10-13. Read-only; every claim needs a source URL with date; mark anything unverifiable UNVERIFIED; British English, no em-dashes, no emojis. Question: can ika-rwth-aachen/mqtt_client v2.5.0 alone carry a Home Assistant MQTT contract for a robot arm, or is a purpose-built ROS 2 node unavoidable? (1) From facontidavide/rosx_introspection source and tests (Parser::deserializeIntoJson, serializeFromJson) and mqtt_client PR #95 tests, document the exact JSON produced for sensor_msgs/msg/JointState, builtin_interfaces/msg/Time, bool, float64[], string[], uint8[] and a nested custom message, and what happens on malformed inbound JSON (crash versus log). List every issue or PR touching JSON mode opened since 2026-07-22. (2) Determine from mqtt_client/src/MqttClient.cpp and README whether a ros2mqtt entry can publish a retained std_msgs/String in primitive mode (advanced.mqtt.retained: true) to homeassistant/device/<id>/config such that HA 2026.10 device-based discovery accepts it, and whether client.last_will with retained: true can serve as an HA availability_topic; cite the HA MQTT discovery and availability docs. (3) Confirm from Paho C/C++ headers and MqttClient.cpp that mqtt_client connects as MQTT 3.1.1, then check Mosquitto 2.1.2 documentation for mixed v3.1.1 and v5 clients (message expiry, retained handling, session behaviour) to settle whether 'MQTT-3-only libraries are ruled out' is correct for a broker that HA talks to over v5. (4) Read eigendude/OASIS issue #1 (comments of 2025-04-01 and 2025-04-22) and mowglinext/mowglinext docs/MQTT_CONTROL.md and extract the concrete reasons each project avoided mqtt_client. (5) If the purpose-built path looks necessary, check paho-mqtt 2.1.0 (PyPI, 2024-04-29) import and test status on Python 3.14 (Ubuntu 26.04 / ROS 2 Lyrical) from the paho.mqtt.python issue tracker and CI. (6) Conclude with a file and approximate line count for each path: mqtt_client YAML plus a minimal action-gateway node, versus one purpose-built rclpy or C++ node with paho; for each path state which functions (discovery, LWT, ack and dedupe, heartbeat watchdog, action lifecycle) still require custom code.

gaps.gap: No direct evidence on the HA side for request/response (ROS 2 action lifecycle) over MQTT, and the MQTT-based custom integration was never evaluated. Every angle's verdict is that a custom integration is only justified if HA must call services or actions synchronously, and angle 5 assumes that integration would ride rosbridge (no authentication). Angle 4 designed a goal/ack/feedback/result MQTT protocol on the assumption that stock HA automations can consume it, but nobody verified that a script can publish a command, wait on an mqtt trigger filtered by command_id with a timeout, and branch on the result (angle 4 itself notes trigger.topic and trigger.payload are not on the reference page it checked). Nobody assessed a thin custom integration built on HA's own MQTT helpers (async_publish, async_subscribe, services with response) that would give typed services, result handling and a device model while keeping broker authentication; angle 2 dismissed it in one clause. The effect of the 2026.10 admin-only mqtt.publish change on scripts run from dashboards is also unassessed.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the fork between 'plain MQTT' and 'custom integration'. If stock HA scripts handle ack and result cleanly, the integration option is dead for this user. If they do not, the right integration is an MQTT-based one, not the rosbridge-based one the research priced and criticised for lacking authentication, which changes the effort, security and maintenance conclusions for that option.
gaps.research_prompt: Research date 2026-10-13, Home Assistant Core 2026.10.x. Read-only; cite URLs with dates; mark unverifiable items UNVERIFIED; British English, no em-dashes, no emojis. Question: can stock Home Assistant run a request/response flow over MQTT well enough to drive a ROS 2 action (publish a goal carrying a command_id, wait for an ack, wait for a result or a timeout, branch on the outcome), and if not, what would a thin custom integration built on HA's MQTT integration look like? (1) From home-assistant.io docs and home-assistant/core source at tag 2026.10.1 (homeassistant/components/mqtt/trigger.py and homeassistant/helpers/script.py), verify the mqtt trigger variables available in templates (trigger.topic, trigger.payload, trigger.payload_json, trigger.qos), wait_for_trigger with an mqtt trigger plus a template condition on payload_json.command_id, timeout and continue_on_timeout, and script response_variable; produce a minimal script that is verified against the docs. (2) Verify how PR #182045 (admin-only mqtt.publish and mqtt.dump, merged 2026-09-14) affects automations without user context, scripts invoked by a non-admin user from a dashboard, and discovery-created MQTT button, select and number entities. (3) Document how a custom integration may use homeassistant.components.mqtt helpers (async_publish, async_subscribe, async_wait_for_mqtt_client, manifest dependencies on mqtt) and register a service with supports_response that awaits a reply; cite developer docs and at least one core integration that depends on mqtt and does request/response over topics (for example tasmota via hatasmota), and list any 2026 developer-blog changes that would affect such an integration. (4) Compare the MQTT event entity, device_trigger and a sensor as carriers for action results, including retained-replay behaviour after HA restart. (5) Conclude: are stock scripts sufficient, yes or no; if a custom integration is warranted, estimate its scope (files, config flow, coordinator, tests, HACS constraints) and whether it should be MQTT-based rather than rosbridge-based.

gaps.gap: The add-on option was only evaluated in its worst form (ROS 2 and DDS inside the container on host_network). Nobody assessed the add-on that avoids DDS entirely: a Supervisor-managed container holding a rosbridge WebSocket client (rosbridge_suite is apt-packaged, maintained, and supports topics, services and actions natively) that translates to HA via Supervisor-provided MQTT credentials or the HA WebSocket API. The Node-RED add-on with the week-old ros2-suite palette was the only hint (angle 3, UNVERIFIED). Nor were the access-control facts behind the transport ranking verified: whether rosbridge can be bound to one interface, run over WSS and firewalled to the HA IP on the ROS host, and whether the HA Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 (Mosquitto 2.1.2, mosquitto-go-auth 3.0.0, acl_file deprecated upstream per angle 6) still enforces per-client topic ACLs via the documented customize route.
gaps.why_it_matters: If a non-ROS bridge-host add-on works, the user gets zero ROS-side code, native action support and independence from HA monthly release churn, which could move the add-on from last place to a serious contender for an HA-centric owner. If broker ACLs cannot be enforced, every existing MQTT client (Zigbee2MQTT, ESPHome, Tasmota) can command the arm, which removes MQTT's main claimed security advantage over rosbridge and changes the safety design regardless of which option is chosen.
gaps.research_prompt: Research date 2026-10-13. Read-only; cite URLs with dates; mark unverifiable items UNVERIFIED; British English, no em-dashes, no emojis. Part A, a Home Assistant add-on with no ROS 2 runtime that runs a rosbridge WebSocket client and translates to MQTT or the HA WebSocket API. (1) From developers.home-assistant.io add-on docs (configuration, communication, Supervisor endpoints): confirm such an add-on can run on the internal network without host_network, obtain Mosquitto credentials via the Supervisor services API, and reach a LAN host on port 9090; note the aarch64/amd64 requirement and the Supervisor 2026.04 BUILD_FROM change. (2) From RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite ros2 branch (4.2.1) and the jazzy and humble releases: confirm the address, ssl, certfile and keyfile, topics_glob, services_glob and action-related launch arguments, whether the server can bind to a single interface, and whether send_action_goal is available on the Humble branch; give the ufw rule that restricts 9090 to one source IP. (3) Find any existing project that packages a rosbridge or roslibpy client as an HA add-on or Docker sidecar, and verify the Node-RED HA add-on route: node-red-contrib-ros2-suite version, publish date, rosbridge dependency and action support from flows.nodered.org or npm. (4) State what such an add-on still needs for a safe arm (the heartbeat watchdog must run on the ROS host; rosbridge has no authentication) and compare its effort with a purpose-built MQTT node on the ROS machine. Part B, Mosquitto add-on access control. (5) From home-assistant/addons mosquitto at master (DOCS.md, config.yaml, the mosquitto.conf and go-auth templates in rootfs) and the mosquitto-go-auth 3.0.0 README: does the documented customize ACL route (acl_file under /share/mosquitto) still apply to HA-user logins and to 'logins' list users on add-on 7.1.1, do the 'homeassistant' and 'addons' users bypass ACLs, and does the Mosquitto 2.1 deprecation of acl_file affect the add-on now or at Mosquitto 3.0. (6) Provide a verified ACL example in which only the ROS credential may publish to robot/+/state and subscribe to robot/+/cmd, and only Home Assistant may publish to robot/+/cmd, and state how it was verified (docs, source or a cited user report).

contradictions: mqtt_client's MQTT protocol version: angle 1 establishes it connects as MQTT 3.1.1 only (Paho default, no v5 setting, no v5 issues or PRs), angle 4 leaves v5 property support UNVERIFIED, and angle 6 states that because HA now requires an MQTT 5 broker the ROS-side client 'should speak MQTT 5 too' and this 'rules out MQTT-3-only libraries', while angles 1 and 5 recommend mqtt_client as the ROS-side bridge. Mixed-version clients on one Mosquitto are normally fine, so angle 6 probably overstates, but the results leave it unresolved.

Fitness of mqtt_client for Home Assistant: angle 1 calls it the clear leader and angle 5's comparison table builds the MQTT row on it; angle 3 reports the OASIS author gave up on it (2025-04-22, before JSON mode) and that MowgliNext, the best current ROS 2 to HA precedent, wrote its own C++ node, and records the lesson that complex ROS schemas do not survive generic JSON bridges. Angles 1 and 3 also agree mqtt_client emits no HA discovery payloads, yet angles 2 and 6 describe the MQTT path as 'the ROS-side bridge publishes one device-discovery payload per arm'.

Effort of the MQTT path: angles 2 and 5 price it as HA-side near zero and ROS-side 'config only' plus 'one small node', whereas angles 3 and 4 enumerate a purpose-built node carrying discovery, retained status plus LWT, command ack and dedupe window, heartbeat watchdog, action gateway and stale-subscription recovery, which is most of the project. The research does not reconcile these two estimates.

Latency and ordering: angle 4 cites sub-millisecond broker latency and 1 to 5 ms LAN round trips and concludes QoS 1 is cheap and ordering is a non-issue; angle 3 reports OASIS observed HA events arriving late, out of order and with jitter over its two-Python-node MQTT path (2025-05-01). Angle 4's own note that Mosquitto max_inflight_messages 1 guarantees in-order delivery is the likely reconciliation but was not tested or tied to the OASIS report.

Who owns HA entity definitions: angle 2 offers three routes (discovery published from ROS 2, hand-made MQTT subentries limited to 21 platforms with no event, update or device_trigger, or manual YAML) and leaves it as a user question; angles 3, 4 and 6 assume device-based discovery from the ROS side as settled. Angle 2 also notes subentries cannot be exported as discovery payloads, so the routes are not interchangeable later.

Kilted Kaiju end of life: angle 1 gives 31 December 2026 (endoflife.date), angle 6 gives December 2026 on the Releases page but November 2026 in the REP 2000 heading. Minor, but it sets the deadline for a distro move if the arm machine is on Kilted.

Add-on viability: angles 2, 3 and 5 rank the add-on last on the premise that it must contain a ROS 2 runtime and join DDS over host_network; angle 3 separately notes a community member would accept 'a standalone app with limited network access' over a HACS integration, and mentions a Node-RED add-on plus rosbridge palette, which is an add-on form that needs no DDS. The results never reconcile these two pictures of what an add-on would be.
